profile.reading:
Per Vantage Data Centers' own facility page, this campus is located at Zgrupowania AK Kampinos 42D, Warsaw, 01-949, Poland. Vantage describes the roughly 12-acre (5-hectare) campus as two four-story buildings totaling 390,000 square feet (36,000 square meters) and 48 megawatts of critical IT load, at an average density of 300 watts per square foot (3.23 kW per square meter), delivered via 480V distribution with N+1 redundancy and stated as 100% concurrently maintainable. Cooling uses closed-loop chilled water with air-side economizers, N+1 overall and N+2 at the component level, with a near-zero water usage effectiveness design. No formal certifications or opening year are stated on the page.

Vantage is a private, Denver, Colorado-headquartered operator with a substantial international footprint across EMEA and APAC in addition to North America; DigitalBridge acquired the company in March 2017, and in January 2024 Vantage announced a $6.4 billion equity investment round led by DigitalBridge and Silver Lake, with Colony Capital, AustralianSuper, GIC, and ADIA cited among its other investors. Warsaw is Poland's largest and most established data center market, drawing hyperscale and colocation investment as Central and Eastern Europe's cloud infrastructure hub, distinct from the US-centric markets tracked elsewhere in this registry.

Warsaw has emerged as a significant Central European data center hub as cloud providers and colocation operators seek EU-jurisdiction capacity outside the traditional FLAP-D markets of Frankfurt, London, Amsterdam, Paris, and Dublin. Poland's data center growth has been supported by Warsaw's position as a national and regional connectivity hub, EU data-residency requirements that have pushed some multinational customers toward in-country capacity, and Poland's power grid operator PSE's ongoing transmission investment as large digital-infrastructure loads grow alongside the country's broader industrial electricity demand. Vantage entered the Warsaw market as part of a broader European expansion that has also included Berlin and other EU metros, positioning WAW1 to serve both domestic Polish enterprise and financial-sector customers and multinational cloud and colocation tenants seeking EU-based capacity.

reading.body:
Warsaw's Vantage WAW1 campus delivers 48 megawatts of critical IT load across 390,000 square feet, making it one of Central Europe's established data center assets outside traditional Western European hubs.

The facility represents the shift of cloud infrastructure investment toward EU-jurisdiction capacity outside Frankfurt, London, Amsterdam, Paris, and Dublin. Poland's data residency requirements and position as a connectivity hub have drawn colocation and hyperscale operators eastward. Warsaw's power grid operator PSE is investing in transmission capacity specifically to support growing digital-infrastructure loads alongside broader industrial demand, directly binding power availability to the region's data center development.

The 48-megawatt campus operates at 300 watts per square foot, a moderate density that reflects mixed-use colocation rather than hyperscale density. Cooling relies on closed-loop chilled water with economizers and near-zero water usage effectiveness, standard for European operators facing water scarcity constraints. The facility's N+1 overall redundancy and stated concurrent maintainability meet enterprise and financial-sector requirements typical of Central European markets.

This registry covers only US-based facilities and includes WAW1 for regional context. The data does not disclose the facility's opening year, current utilization rate, or tenant composition, limiting assessment of its role in Poland's infrastructure demand curve or its contribution to broader European AI workload distribution.
